name: parallelization
context: Tasks where independent LLM calls can run concurrently to reduce wall-clock time, or where multiple independent attempts provide higher confidence through diversity. Useful when the task can be cleanly split into subtasks that do not depend on each other's outputs, or when the same task benefits from multiple independent perspectives.
benefits: Reduces wall-clock latency by running independent calls concurrently
Catches outliers and errors through majority-voting across attempts
Enables focused, single-purpose prompts per worker for better quality
Scales throughput linearly with independent subtasks
tradeoffs: Adds coordination overhead for result aggregation
Redundant work when tasks share intermediate results
Increased total token cost vs. sequential single-pass when tasks overlap
use_cases: Sectioning: parallel document processing where each section is independent
Sectioning: running guardrails on input while the main LLM processes content
Voting: multiple model instances reviewing the same code for different vulnerability classes
Voting: sentiment analysis with different perspectives to catch outliers
avoid_when: Subtasks have data dependencies requiring sequential execution
Cost is the primary constraint and quality tolerance is high
Task outputs are expensive to produce redundantly
anti_patterns: Running all workers on the same input with identical prompts (no diversity gain)
Failing to handle worker timeouts gracefully
Aggregating results without checking for consensus
No result schema validation in aggregator
Shared output keys causing race conditions
design_principles: Workers must be stateless — no shared mutable state between workers
Aggregation must be deterministic or use explicit voting logic
Fan-out is only worthwhile when wall-clock savings exceed coordination overhead
best_practices: Set explicit per-worker timeouts and aggregate partial results on timeout
Use diverse system prompts or model variants for voting to maximize coverage
Validate that tasks are truly independent before choosing this pattern
Use Promise.allSettled over Promise.all so one failure does not crash entire run
Use Semaphore sized to requests-per-minute with exponential backoff for 429s
Validate result schema in aggregator parent, not child workers
Cap parallel subagent spawns with concurrency limit; queue excess with backpressure
references: Anthropic, Building Effective Agents: Parallelization workflow, Dec 2024 — https://www.anthropic.com/engineering/building-effective-agents
